stem:
Inhibitors are substances that prevent biological processes in a variety of different ways.

Table 5.1 shows some antibiotics, their modes of action and the diseases which they are used to treat.

Table 5.1

| antibiotic | mode of action | disease |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| erythromycin | binds to ribosomes to inhibit translation | cholera |
| penicillin | enzyme inhibitor | tetanus |
| rifampicin | inhibits the function of RNA polymerase in transcription | tuberculosis |

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest why erythromycin can inhibit translation in the bacterium that causes cholera **and not** inhibit translation in humans who are infected with this pathogen.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: State why penicillin does **not** act on human cells.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain **one** way in which rifampicin may inhibit the action of RNA polymerase in transcription.
